title: Choose the visual world
question: Re-roll 1 assigned Bench Notebook. Keep it, take my pick or the category standard, or re-roll again.

options.label: Bench Notebook
options.lineage: engineering computation pads and dated lab notebooks
options.thesis: The portfolio is the engineer's own notebook sheet: work taped in, results annotated, every entry dated.
materials: pale green computation paper with grid
options.viewport: A notebook sheet whose title block is the nav; the name is lettered across the grid and project prints are taped over its edge.
options.risk: Tips into scrapbook kitsch if tape and annotations appear everywhere instead of where proof lives.

raised.raise: Each view keeps one primary print and leaves a charged field of empty grid.
Dates are the structural ruler: every entry hangs off one tabular date rule.
Absent states are designed: a missing screenshot shows a labelled 'print pending' frame.
Motion obeys paper physics: tape tension, sheet weight, settle, never arbitrary easing.
Closer inspection rewards: hovering a print reveals its annotations, never required to understand.
Annotation size maps to impact; the biggest result gets the biggest note.

options.label: Sticker Lid
options.lineage: engineers' laptop lids covered in die-cut stickers
options.thesis: Every project is a die-cut sticker on the engineer's laptop lid.
options.viewport: A brushed aluminium lid full-bleed; the name is a vinyl lettering sticker, projects are stickers around it.
options.risk: Laptop stickers are the first idea many dev portfolios reach for when they want personality.

options.label: Ikebana Ma
options.thesis: Three projects arranged as primary, secondary, supporting stems.
options.viewport: An alcove with one dominant project print.
options.case: Fuses as a sparse showcase, but recruiters gain nothing from the metaphor.

options.label: Daylight Section
options.thesis: A career read as rooms lit by moving light.
options.viewport: One long building section with years as light bands.
options.case: Fuses as a timeline with mood; recruiters do not read sections.

options.label: Seven-Segment
options.thesis: Career stats lit on a scoreboard mask.
options.viewport: A scoreboard of years, projects, wins.
options.case: Fuses into stat theatre and the dark-tech rut; hides the work.

options.label: Ink Basin
options.thesis: The page is a liquid surface the cursor stirs.
options.viewport: A marbled basin with the name in the still margin.
options.case: Fuses as a WebGL toy; heavy and unrelated to shipped work.

options.label: Pixorama City
options.thesis: Projects as buildings in a zoomable pixel city.
options.viewport: A pixel city block with project buildings.
options.case: Fuses as a playful map, but screenshots cannot live in its pixel grid.

options.label: Telop Captions
options.thesis: Outlined captions shout the highlights over the work.
options.viewport: Project video with captions sized by excitement.
options.case: Fuses as loud overlays; undermines a professional read.

canonCard.label: The category standard
canonCard.thesis: A clean developer portfolio, executed carefully.
canonCard.viewport: Name and role top-left, a short bio, a project grid, experience list.
canonCard.risk: Indistinguishable from every other engineer's site by design.
